context: HALTED AT THE CANARY — deliberately, before the browser suites. Canary ran 2 of 050d's 49 cases: new PRF-GQL-077 and, as a control, PRE-EXISTING PRF-GQL-047. BOTH fail identically: organization(id: TechFlow) returns Access denied / Forbidden INSIDE HTTP 200 for TECHFLOW_ADMIN. TECHFLOW_ADMIN = b2b/users USR-006 = ORG_USER = test-emily.johnson (userId 68fed13a) — the very user whose TechFlow membership carries status=Rejected in fixture-snapshot.json, while her currentOrganizationId IS TechFlow. So her token grant still returns 200 (td:reconcile check [10] passes) and every org-scoped query then 403s: the VCST-5281 P0 root cause, reproduced deterministically on canonical fixture data, and it takes down pre-existing coverage too. Suites 027/008/011b all authenticate as this same user against this same org, so continuing would have rediscovered one blocker across ~150 cases and misattributed the failures. No fixture was mutated by this run. Also found: td:reconcile does NOT validate OrganizationMembership.Status against the declared fixture status, so this drift vector is invisible to the reconciler.

VCST-5281 regression. 050d complete (32/49) with the shared-fixture leak CLOSED — PRF-GQL-076/079/081 were rewritten to be self-contained (own throwaway org/user) after 076 upserted the canonical ORG_USER membership and 079 restored it with HARDCODED status Approved + roleId org-employee over its real null/org-maintainer values. Canonical membership verified intact after the full run. Now dispatching the browser suites sequentially: 027 (edge) then 008 (chrome) then 011b (chrome) — never batched, because 008+011b both mutate TechFlow and 027 shares the same org-maintainer actor.
